Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Quick update on Vivian Cho (senior inference engineer). She just sent a counter: base 205k + guaranteed 35k sign-on (cash), and they want an equity refresh of 0.18% (targeted 4 year vesting ramp). Comp band shows this is outside our posted band for Senior Inference (band midpoint 170k — 200k). Vivian has a strong systems + quant background, several architecture wins at her current employer, and a competing offer from VectorML with an aggressive start timeline (they asked for a decision by Friday).

Ask: can Redwood approve an out-of-band uplift to 205k base, a 35k one-time sign-on (prorated if <12 months), and a one-time equity refresh of 0.18% to be added to the base grant?

Rationale (attached): short market comp memo + candidate summary. If we lose her, we expect an engineering delay on the LLM routing project (E2E latency improvements) estimated at 6-8 weeks. Vivian has lead experience on kernel-level perf work and would remove a critical hiring blocker.

Attachments: candidate_CompProposal.pdf (proposal), market_comp_benchmarks.xlsx

Preferred timing: we need an approval conversation today so we can get the DocuSign over by EOD and meet VectorML's timeline.

Alex

Thanks for the context, Jonas. A few quick questions before I can sign off operationally:
1) Band exceptions: is this a permanent band uplift or a one-time out-of-band offer? (I assume one-time; prefer keeping band governance intact.)
2) Equity: how is the 0.18% structured — is this a top-up on the standard grant or a separate refresh grant? Will this require board approval or is it covered under existing grant delegated authority?
3) Sign-on clawback: you suggested 9 months — legal/finance prefer 12 months historically. Can we split the difference to 10 months prorate?

If we keep it one-time and structure equity as a refresh grant approved by delegated authority, I am inclined to approve the request given the project risk. Need Finance to confirm cash budget.
